quotes.text: We used chamber-pots a good deal – ‘jerries’ – cause of much hilarity doe to the hostilities.
quotes.reference: 1976, Angela Carter, “The Mother Lode”, in Shaking a Leg, Vintage, published 2013, page 3:

quotes.text: If a man builds a jerry-house, he has a jerry conscience; and there are a lot of consciences of that description going about.
quotes.reference: 1889, Alfred Thomas Story, A book of vagrom men and vagrant thoughts, page 57:

senses.definition: (ethnic slur) Alternative letter-case form of Jerry (“a German”).

examples:
R. Austin Freeman, A Savant's Vendetta
'Do you know a jerry when you sees one — a red 'un, mind you?' […] The fellow looked furtively at the door and then, diving into an inner pocket, pulled out a handsome gold watch with a massive chain attached, exhibited it for a moment and then dropped it back.

quotes.text: Watch stealing, or jerry getting, as the thieving fraternity designate the operation, is carried on to a considerable extent all the year round.
